For the treatment of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), the preferred regimen includes Clindamycin at a dose of 150–600 mg administered intravenously (IV), intramuscularly (IM), or orally (PO) every 6–8 hours. The maximum dose is 5 g per 24 hours for IV or IM administration, or 2 g per 24 hours for oral administration. Alternatively, Linezolid 600 mg IV or PO every 12 hours can be used, combined with Vancomycin at a dose of 15–20 mg/kg IV every 8–12 hours, not exceeding 2 g per dose. Teicoplanin may also be considered. 2. An alternative regimen for MRSA includes Rifampicin combined with Linezolid 600 mg IV or PO every 12 hours, or Daptomycin, or Tigecycline with a 100 mg loading dose followed by 50 mg IV every 12 hours. 3. For glycopeptide-resistant or intermediate Staphylococcus aureus, the preferred regimen is Linezolid 600 mg IV or PO every 12 hours, combined with Clindamycin 150–600 mg IV, IM, or PO every 6–8 hours (maximum dose: 5 g/24 hours IV or IM, or 2 g/24 hours PO), if the strain is sensitive. 4. An alternative regimen for glycopeptide-resistant Staphylococcus aureus includes Daptomycin or Tigecycline with a 100 mg loading dose followed by 50 mg IV every 12 hours. 5. For prophylaxis of coronary artery bypass graft-associated acute mediastinitis caused by methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA), a firstor second-generation cephalosporin is recommended in patients without MRSA colonization. 6. For MRSA prophylaxis in the same context, Vancomycin alone or in combination with other antibiotics to achieve broader coverage is recommended for patients with proven or suspected MRSA colonization. 7. For coagulase-negative Staphylococcus (CoNS) infections, such as Staphylococcus epidermidis or Staphylococcus haemolyticus, bacteremia is often associated with IV lines, vascular grafts, or cardiac valves, accounting for 30–40% of all CoNS infections. The preferred regimen includes Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV every 12 hours, with or without Rifampin 300 mg IV/PO every 8 hours, or Gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV every 8 hours. For prosthetic valve infective endocarditis (IE), Vancomycin and Rifampin 300 mg IV/PO every 8 hours are added. 8. An alternative regimen for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis includes Linezolid 600 mg IV/PO twice daily or Daptomycin IV 6 mg/kg/day, with or without Rifampin 300 mg IV/PO every 8 hours. 9. For methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus epidermidis, alternative options include Oxacillin 1.5–3 g IV every 6 hours, Nafcillin 1.5–3 g IV every 6 hours, Cefazolin 1–2 g IV every 8 hours, Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV every 12 hours, Clindamycin 600 mg IV every 8 hours, or Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole. 10. For cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) shunt-associated meningitis, the preferred regimen includes Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV every 12 hours, with or without Rifampin 300 mg IV/PO every 8 hours, or Gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV every 8 hours. For prosthetic valve IE, Vancomycin and Rifampin 300 mg IV/PO every 8 hours are added. 11. For peritoneal dialysis catheter-associated peritonitis, the same regimens as above are recommended. 12. For prosthetic joint septic arthritis, the preferred regimen includes Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV every 12 hours, with or without Rifampin 300 mg IV/PO every 8 hours, or Gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV every 8 hours, added to Vancomycin and Rifampin 300 mg IV/PO every 8 hours for prosthetic valve IE. 13. For post-sternotomy osteomyelitis, the same regimens as above are recommended. 14. For infections involving implants (e.g., breast, penile, pacemaker) or other prosthetic devices, the same regimens as above are recommended. 15. For post-ocular surgery endophthalmitis, the same regimens as above are recommended. 16. For surgical site infections, the same regimens as above are recommended.
